title: Sequence stability oracle and runtime harmonizer
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: build a compact, repeatable test harness (the 'sequence stability oracle') and a small runtime harmonizer that can be run in CI to validate end-to-end behavior across streaming, function/tool invocation, and structured-output code paths. This ticket covers test design, harness implementation, CI pipeline integration, and a lightweight runtime shim that intentionally exercises compatibility fallbacks used in production routing.

Why: recent incidents showed subtle divergences between model streaming behavior and the tool-call framing (partial JSON fragments, interleaved metadata tokens, and boundary KV cache priming differences). We need an automated, fast-smoke validation that catches regressions before rollout and provides clear finger-prints for SRE/QA to triage.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- A reproducible harness that runs as a unit in the monorepo CI (15m max) and a longer nightly job for broader coverage.
- Test corpus: curated seed prompts + perturbation generator (token-boundary mutations, intentional latency jitter, and payload truncation scenarios).
- Hooks to exercise: streaming partial chunks, tool/function call initiation and mid-stream tool interrupts, structured JSON schema emission, and graceful fallback to ndjson/line-delimited variants.
- A small runtime harmonizer binary (language: Go) that can simulate older/newer kernel behaviors to test compatibility routing/fallback policies.
- Clear failure classification: flakiness, schema drift, non-deterministic interleaving, and latency-induced partial-output.
- CI gating: harness must block canary deploy for runtime-1.22 if new failures appear; failures produce a triage ticket template and attach canonical artifacts (chat transcript, raw tokens, seed id).

Test design notes and trade-offs:
- We prioritize speed in the CI smoke run: use a narrow seed set that covers diverse edgecases rather than exhaustive golden corpus. The nightly job will run the exhaustive seeds.
- Use perturbation generator rather than an enormous list of golden prompts to surface brittle assumptions in prompt parsing. This is more likely to find boundary bugs introduced by kernel scheduling changes.
- Runtime harmonizer intentionally omits heavy model execution; it focuses on I/O surface behaviors so it can be run on CI runners without GPUs.
- Fallback simulation: harmonizer will emulate model variants that emit partial JSON messages mid-stream to ensure the streaming parser and tool invocation reconciler recover properly. This avoids creating fragile PR requirements around heavyweight model images.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype perturbation generator and 12-seed base prompts (week 1).
2) Implement streaming + tool-call smoke scenarios in harness (week 2).
3) Build Go runtime harmonizer binary and local runner (week 3).
4) Wire the harness into monorepo CI with a 15-minute smoke job; add nightly matrix job (week 4).
5) Add triage automation that opens templated Linear tickets with artifacts on failure (post-merge).

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Drive): https://drive.redwood.company/sequence-stability-oracle (proto draft)
- Reference PR pattern: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/PRs (will attach specific PRs when created)
- Observability dashboard to link: Console -> /dashboards/sequence-stability (placeholder)

Risks and mitigation:
- Flaky CI: mitigate by stable seeds, deterministic RNG with explicit seed logging, and failure classification thresholds.
- Noise from model drift: nightly exhaustive job will separate drift regressions from deterministic breaks.
- Overlap with existing compliance tests: coordinate with QA owners (cc: @Carla Nguyen) to avoid duplication.

Success metrics:
- Smoke CI reduces post-deploy streaming/tool regressions by 80% in the next quarter.
- Mean time to triage for failures < 48h due to attached canonical artifacts.
- Nightly job catches regressions introduced by kernel/quantization changes before they reach canary stage.
